entries.search: about this wiki the wiki is available in two places with the same articles: in the game: the wiki button on the main menu and on the game files screen, the wiki button under the etherlords ii esc menus in battle and on the map, or shift+f1 on any screen. the game waits while you read. esc, f1 or close returns to it. on the web at demiurges.wwworm.com/wiki, free to read without game files, an account or the engine. the browser version's start page links to it. languages every article is written in english and russian. switch with en / ru at the top of the in-game wiki or with the language list on the website. your choice is remembered. until you choose, the in-game wiki follows the language of your game's texts and the website follows your browser. names of game things (races, phases, menus) follow the original games' own english and russian texts where they apply. what it covers the guides explain how to play the games on this engine and how the engine differs from the originals. the encyclopedia has a page for every creature, sorcery, enchantment, artifact, skill and specialization of both games, with its statistics, prices and description. on the website, creature pages show a picture of the creature; in the game they show the creature itself, which you can turn and zoom. the encyclopedia in the game is built from your own copy, so it follows your game's language and data. the website's encyclopedia was exported from the original russian and english (gog) editions. names, descriptions and pictures of the games' content belong to their owners. to preview attacks, hit reactions, deaths, and other actions with their original sounds, press shift+f1 in the game and open a creature page. choose an action below the 3d model and press play. see about creatures for the full controls.

entries.search: about creatures creatures are summoned with creature spells and fight for their hero. power and toughness each creature has power, the damage it deals in combat, and toughness, the damage it can take. damage on a creature heals at the end of each turn, so a creature is destroyed only when it takes as much damage as its toughness within one turn. resting a creature that attacks or uses certain abilities rests and stays down until its owner's next turn. a newly summoned creature also rests unless it has haste. resting creatures cannot block. abilities most creatures have abilities, shown as icons. see creature abilities for the common ones and attack and defence for how they affect combat. limits a hero can control at most 10 creatures. destroyed creatures go to their owner's graveyard; some spells bring them back. all creatures of both games: the list of creatures. preview animations and sounds press f1 in the game and open a page from the creature list. use the menu below the 3d model to choose an animation, then press play. depending on the creature, you can preview attacks, ranged attacks, hit reactions, deaths, and other actions. to return to the idle pose, select idle and press play again. drag the model to turn it and scroll to zoom. when the page offers models for both games, choose etherlords i or etherlords ii to see the animations available in that edition. the viewer plays the original creature sounds when a recording is available. it uses the effects volume from options. the web wiki shows still images of creatures.

entries.search: how a battle works every battle in etherlords is a duel between two heroes, the etherlords. each hero casts spells from a spellbook: creatures fight, enchantments change the battle and sorceries act at once. the first hero whose health falls to 0 loses. demiurges follows the original rules of each game; the same structure applies to both games, with differences in the numbers. health a hero's health grows with the hero's level. the strength skill adds 10, 20 or 30%. in campaign battles the hero starts with the health they have on the map. if both heroes reach 0 at the same moment, the battle is a draw. ether and ether channels spells cost ether. each hero has ether channels, which start at 0 and grow by 0 to 2 at the start of every turn, faster for higher-level heroes. each turn the hero's ether is refilled to the number of channels, so ether you do not spend is lost. some etherlords ii spells also need a minimum number of channels, and spells with a variable cost take as much extra ether as you choose. ether disturbance stops a battle from dragging on: after a number of turns that grows with the hero's level, the hero starts losing health every turn. in etherlords the damage grows by 1 each turn; in etherlords ii it grows much faster. the channeling skill delays your own disturbance and hastens your opponent's. the hand and the spellbook both heroes start with 5 spells in hand, dealt in turn. after that, every turn starts with one draw (the side that begins does not draw on the very first turn). extra draws come from the concentration skill and some spells. at the end of your turn you keep at most 5 spells. spells are drawn at random from the spellbook, without repeats until every spell in the book has been drawn. how often a spell can be used differs between the games: see runes and artifacts. creatures a hero controls at most 10 creatures. a newly summoned creature rests: it cannot attack or use abilities that need it to rest until its owner's next turn, unless it has haste. damage on creatures heals at the end of every turn; destroyed creatures go to their owner's graveyard. see creatures and creature abilities. next turn and phases: what happens in which order. attack and defence: how attackers, blockers and damage work. spells: the three kinds of spell.

entries.search: turn and phases a turn belongs to one hero, the attacker. it has two phases: the attacker's attack/cast phase, then the opponent's block phase. then the heroes swap roles and the next turn begins. use the end of phase button, ctrl+e in etherlords, or tab in etherlords ii to finish your phase. space skips the current presentation. start of the turn at the start of the attacker's turn, in this order: ether disturbance damage, once it has started. healing from the regeneration skill. the attacker's creatures recover (stand up) and stop being newly summoned, except under spells that keep them down. the attacker draws a spell. ether channels grow and ether is refilled to the number of channels. enchantments that act at the start of the turn take effect. attack/cast phase the attacker casts spells and chooses which ready creatures attack. creatures that rest, were just summoned (without haste) or cannot attack stay back. berserk creatures must attack. when the attacker ends the phase, the chosen creatures attack. if no creature attacks, the block phase is skipped. block phase now the defender acts: they assign blockers (and may cast the few spells allowed in this phase) to the attacking creatures. each ready creature can block one attacker, and several creatures can block the same attacker. when the defender ends the phase, combat damage is dealt: see attack and defence. end of the turn the attacker discards down to 5 spells in hand. damage on all creatures heals. enchantments that act at the end of the turn take effect. who begins in a duel, a coin decides who attacks first in every round. in campaign battles the map decides, as in the original games. in the attack/cast phase you can cast any spell you can pay for. in the block phase only a few spells are allowed, as in the original games: polymorph, fog and energize all, and two more in etherlords ii. each card that allows it says so in its description.

entries.search: attack and defence creatures fight in the phases of a turn: the attacker chooses attackers in the attack/cast phase, the defender chooses blockers in the block phase, and then damage is dealt. who can attack a creature can attack if it is ready (not resting) and was not summoned this turn, unless it has haste. these cannot attack: creatures that cannot attack, such as walls; creatures held back by battlefield spells, for example spells that stop weak creatures; in etherlords ii, creatures in their pale aspect. berserk creatures attack whenever they can and cannot be withdrawn. a team attacker attacks only together with a creature of its own race. attacking creatures rest afterwards unless they are restless. blocking in the block phase every ready defending creature may block one attacker, and several creatures can block the same attacker, in the order you assign them. limits: only a flying creature can block a flying creature; an unblockable creature cannot be blocked; an elusive creature (etherlords ii) can only be blocked by walls. damage an unblocked attacker deals its power to the defending hero. a blocked attacker shares its power among its blockers in order, giving each as much as it needs to be destroyed before moving on to the next. every blocker strikes back with its own power. a creature with first strike hits first; if its opponent is destroyed, the opponent does not hit back. a trample attacker sends the damage left over after destroying its blockers on to the hero. damage on surviving creatures heals at the end of the turn. a hero's specialisation can add chance-based effects in combat; the hero's luck and the opponent's suppression change the odds. see creature abilities for more abilities.

abilities every original creature ability works in real time, adapted so that it is fair at every star level: first strike opens each fight with a stronger blow and delays the enemy's swing. regeneration heals only after two seconds without taking damage. poison of snakes deals extra damage over time instead of killing outright. deadly venom of hornets and mechanoids finishes an enemy that is still badly wounded a few seconds later, but never a three-star or 5-cost creature. flying, trample, vampire, bloodthirsty, unblockable and breaks enchantments keep their meaning. active abilities (dragon breath, the cyclops' strike, mantis fright, revivals and auras) recharge during battle. alliances deploying different lines of one kind gives a bonus to all of them: chaots 2 / 4 / 6 +10 / 20 / 30% attack damage kinets 2 / 4 faster ability recharge and attacks vitals 2 / 4 1 / 2% health per second synthets 2 / 4 +3 / 6 defense flyers 2 / 4 evade 15 / 30% of attacks from the ground first strike 2 / 4 +30 / 60% opening blow spells and artifacts rewards are etherlords ii enchantments and artifacts in five tiers. each one is given to a single creature: attack and health bonuses, lifetap, shadow cloak, haste, the rods of fire, lightning and colossus, the ring of command and others. click a reward, then a creature, to give it. controls click a reserve creature, then the ground, to deploy it; drag a creature to move it. right-click a creature or offer for details. s sells the selected creature, ctrl+z undoes the last purchase or move. w a s d move the camera, q e or entries.search: custom maps maps made with the etherlords ii map editor play like the shipped missions. they are listed in single → mission after the game's own maps. a chosen map shows its picture above the description and plays its own music. adding a map on the mission screen, import map… takes a map's .zip archive and copies the map into the remake's maps folder. the map is chosen at once. maps folder opens that folder. copy a map's files into it, or into a folder of their own inside it, then open the mission screen again. maps the editor saved into the game's own maps\custom folder are listed too. the maps folder is maps inside the folder where saves are kept (see main menu, saves and settings). what a map consists of a map is a set of files that share its name: .smp the scenario: terrain, objects, players, heroes and creatures .sbm the map file with its title and description .scp scripts: the map's own story and the battle scripts of its creatures .bm1 the minimap .png, .bmp, .bm2 pictures; the first one found is shown on the mission screen .mp3 music played while the map is chosen the .smp is what the remake plays. a map with only a .sbm is listed with a note and cannot be started; a map with only a .smp plays and takes its title from the scenario. when a map's .smp and .sbm are named differently but are the only two in their folder, they count as one map. scripts may sit in sub-folders: a map that names maps\custom\ctt\hero.scp finds ctt\hero.scp next to it. all custom maps share these names, so two maps with a script of the same name and folder use the same file. an import copies only these files from the archive, keeping their sub-folders, and ignores everything else. scripts a map's scripts are plain lua text written for the original game. the remake compiles them when the map starts and runs them with the same commands as the shipped missions. if a script stops with an error, the message names the script and the line; please report such a map together with its archive (see troubleshooting). scripts may use the original game's map commands that no shipped mission calls: scripted hero animations, point lights, camera pitch and scroll queries, and reading or removing commands in the queue. their arguments are not documented, so they follow the related commands; a map that uses one differently may look different from the original. saves a save of a custom map records which map it belongs to. it loads only while that map is in place and unchanged: a missing map or one whose files changed since the save (an updated version, for example) is reported instead of loaded.

entries.search: installing the game files demiurges reads the files of a game you own. it needs either game, or both: each game keeps its own rules, files and saves. nothing is downloaded for you and no game content comes with the engine. download the engine get the package for your system from the releases page, or play in the browser without installing anything. windows (x86-64) extract the zip and run demiurges.exe. smartscreen may warn about an unrecognised app: choose more info → run anyway. linux (x86-64) extract the archive and run demiurges.x86_64. if needed, run chmod +x demiurges.x86_64 first. macos extract the zip and open demiurges.app. the app is not signed: right-click it and choose open, or allow it under system settings → privacy & security. android 7+ install the apk and allow your browser or file manager to install apps when asked. add a game at the first start the game files screen opens. choose etherlords i or etherlords ii at its top, then one of: the game folder: the folder of your installed game, the one containing resources and campaigns; the gog offline installer (setup_etherlords.exe). it is not run: the engine unpacks the game files from it once and keeps them in its own data folder, so you do not need the installer afterwards; a data pack (.elpack, see below). steam copies are found automatically on windows, linux and macos: at the first start the engine uses any it finds, and the game files screen offers use the steam copy for a game not set up yet. your choice is remembered. the original start-up videos play and then the main menu opens. repeat this for the other game to keep both. data packs a data pack holds the files of one game in a single file. it is useful on a phone that has neither the installer nor the game folder: make the pack on your computer with the prepare_game_data.py script from the project (it needs python 3) and copy it to the phone: python3 prepare_game_data.py "/path/to/etherlords ii" etherlords2.elpack the installer and the data pack contain your own game files. keep them to yourself. adding, switching and removing games options › remake settings › game files… opens the same screen at any time to add a game, switch to another one or remove one. removing a game keeps its saves and settings and never deletes an installed game folder.

entries.search: playing in the browser the browser version runs at demiurges.wwworm.com. there is nothing to install: open the page, press play and give it your game files. giving it your game files choose one of: the gog offline installer (setup_etherlords.exe). it is not run: the browser unpacks the game files from it once and checks each one. this takes a few minutes and needs about 1.5 gb (etherlords) or 3 gb (etherlords ii) of browser storage; the folder of your installed game, in desktop browsers; a data pack (.elpack). repeat this for the other game to keep both. your files are never uploaded: the game reads them on your own device and keeps its copy in the browser's storage, so the next start is quick. requirements webgl 2 and a desktop-class browser, or a recent phone with plenty of memory. unpacking a large game needs a lot of memory for a short time; if it fails on a phone, use a data pack. intro and ending videos are not played in the browser yet. browsers can clear their storage. keep your installer or pack, and remember that clearing the site's data also removes your saves. this wiki the wiki you are reading is part of the same site at demiurges.wwworm.com/wiki and is also built into the game: see about this wiki.

entries.search: main menu, saves and settings the main menu is the original game's menu. under its buttons the remake adds etherlords i and etherlords ii: click one to switch games, or wiki to open this wiki. the game you played last opens at the next start. a game you have not added yet says not installed — add… and opens the game files screen for it. from the wiki, open a creature's page to play its attacks, death, and other animations with sound. what the menu offers etherlords: new game (duel, campaign, single mission), load game, options, hall of fame, credits and quit. see duel. etherlords ii: single (tutorial, duel, campaign, mission, which also lists custom maps), multiplayer (network and hot seat duels), options, encyclopedia, credits and quit. with etherlords ii installed, the remake adds autochess beside the game choice. saves saving and loading use the original screens. f5 saves quickly and f9 loads the quick save, on the map and in battle. saves of the original games cannot be loaded; the engine keeps its own, separately for each game. where saves and settings are kept windows %appdata%\godot\app_userdata\etherlords duel linux ~/.local/share/godot/app_userdata/etherlords duel macos ~/library/application support/godot/app_userdata/etherlords duel browser the browser's storage for the site; clearing the site's data removes them android the app's private storage; uninstalling the app removes them the folder keeps its earlier name, etherlords duel, so older saves continue to work.

entries.search: differences from the originals demiurges follows the rules of the original games. it runs on modern systems and changes only what this page lists. added both games in one program, switched from the main menu, each with its own rules, saves and settings. windows, linux, macos, android and the browser; touch controls. remake settings: soft shadows, terrain detail, sharpening, anti-aliasing and more. the automatic camera can be interrupted by moving the camera yourself. this wiki, in english and russian, in the game and on the web. not available gamespy and full strategic multiplayer. native builds offer network duels and a strategic preview. loading saves of the original games. original etherlords ii replays can be watched. intro and ending videos in the browser. not yet exact computer opponents follow the original's approach but are not an exact copy of its decisions. the darkening of a few large spells, the timing of some ability effects and etherlords ii map particles are approximations. the remake's own screens follow the language of your game. a few rare error messages and the battle log are still in english. kept on purpose some behaviour of the originals looks like a mistake but is kept because the games work that way: the etherlords skills ethereal attack and ethereal defense do nothing. random battle events of etherlords never happen, as in the original. several etherlords global spells only cost upkeep. as in the originals, computer players never answer alliance or trade offers. see problems and reporting for known gaps.

entries.search: problems and reporting demiurges is still in development. these are the things you are most likely to notice. known gaps a few rare error messages and the battle log are still shown in english. computer opponents follow the original's approach but do not copy its decisions exactly. as in the original, they never answer alliance or trade offers. the campaigns are tested screen by screen and system by system, not yet by playing every chapter from start to finish. network duels use the host's address. the browser build supports local hot seat. touch controls have only been tried in testing, not yet on many real phones. the interface keeps the original layout, so on a small phone text and buttons are small. intro and ending videos are not played in the browser yet. if the game does not start check that you chose the folder that contains resources and campaigns, or the gog offline installer. see installing the game files. in the browser, make sure the page has enough storage and memory; on a phone, try a data pack. on windows and macos, allow the unsigned app as described in installing the game files. reporting a problem report problems on the issues page. say which game and which system you use, and what you did before the problem appeared.
